item.title: #3586412: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Text-To-Image Generation Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 13 files, +2770/−236 · php +1859/−234 · css +531 · js +360 · yml +10 · twig +9/−1 · md +1/−1
  • Diff: 72b6a5e
  • Discussion: #3586412 · 1 contributor · 19 comments

Summary

The Text to Image explorer in AI API Explorer has been rebuilt on the shared explorer layout. The prompt and settings sit on the left and results on the right. Size is picked from shape tiles, and the number of images is a stepper. Quality and format are segmented controls. Each run is kept with its prompt and settings when run history is on, and shows progress while generating. Images open in a preview with download, use as source in Image to image, and save to media library. On phones the settings open in a bottom sheet. Generated files now get the extension that matches the real image format (PNG, JPEG or WebP) instead of always .png, and the code example no longer calls a nonexistent method.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: ai-api-explorer-image.html.twig renders a .aie-lightbox__head wrapper with an optional title_label and title_actions around the title.
  • New API: ExplorerUi::image() and the image viewer template accept title_label and title_actions options.

Technical details

TextToImageGenerator now builds its form on the shared layout and replaces AiProviderFormHelper::generateAiProvidersForm() with the ai_provider_configuration element via providerElement(). The size, quality, format and count fields are filled in by processImageSettings() from the selected model's definition and replaced when the model changes. Every size the provider lists for the model is offered. The code does not disable sizes the model cannot make, and says so in a comment: a size the model refuses shows as an error on the run, and a size the model adjusts shows as the size that came back. The OpenAI 1792x1024 and 1024x1792 listing and the missing auto size are not fixed here, as the issue says this needs a follow-up in the provider.

The file extension and MIME type are detected from the image data first, then from the provider's file name (imageType()), and are used for the saved run file, the download and the media entity. The code example is generated per run in buildRunCode(). It uses getRawOutput() and the real extension. Save to media uses a hidden submit button filled in by text_to_image.js, it only works for the current user's runs, it is disabled with a reason when media cannot be created, and saving an image twice does not create a second media item.

The shared image viewer gets title_label and title_actions options (ExplorerUi::image(), the default in AiApiExplorer, and ai-api-explorer-image.html.twig). A new explorer.text_to_image library holds the CSS and JS. The ai_api_explorer_test module gains a test text to image provider, and a functional test covers generation, formats and media saving. The docs now give the new explorer path /admin/config/ai/explorers/text_to_image_generator. AiApiExplorerInterface::getAjaxResponseId() documentation now allows a static method.

item.title: #3586406: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Summarize Text Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 7 files, +819/−120 · php +727/−120 · css +48 · js +36 · yml +8
  • Diff: ba4dabd
  • Discussion: #3586406 · 1 contributor · 14 comments

Summary

The Summarize Text Explorer in AI API Explorer has been rebuilt on the shared explorer layout. It now has instruction presets (One sentence, 3 bullet points, For a newsletter) next to the free-text instructions field. Each summary shows how much shorter (or longer) it is than the source, as bars and a percentage. Every run stays in the Results region with its instructions, newest first, and failures show next to their run. Each run also gets a generated code example.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

SummarizationGenerator now builds on buildLayout() and replaces AiProviderFormHelper::generateAiProvidersForm() with the ai_provider_configuration element via providerElement('summarize', ...). Submission goes through executeRun(), which stores the text, instructions and provider value as the run input and the summary as output. The provider is created with createProviderFromValue(). An empty summary is stored as an error with the message 'The provider returned no summary.' Results are rendered from stored runs by buildRunResults() and the runTitle(), runBadge(), runActions() and buildRunOutput() overrides. The summary text is escaped with Html::escape().

The length comparison in buildLength() counts words, or characters when the source averages more than 20 characters per word (text without spaces, such as Chinese). The code example per run comes from buildRunCode() using the CodeExample builder. The presets are filled in by a new explorer.summarize library (css/explorers/summarize.css, js/explorers/summarize.js). The preset buttons are rendered hidden and shown by JavaScript, since they only fill the instructions textarea, and they carry aria-pressed state.

The change adds a test-only module plugin, TestSummarizeProvider (ai_api_explorer_test), and a functional test SummarizeExplorerTest. The provider returns the first sentence, or bullets when the instructions mention them, and the texts empty and fail trigger the empty and exception paths.

item.title: #3586408: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Rerank Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 10 files, +1765/−207 · php +1196/−207 · js +305 · css +255 · yml +9
  • Diff: ae33214
  • Discussion: #3586408 · 1 contributor · 12 comments

Summary

The Rerank Explorer in the AI API Explorer module has been rebuilt on the shared explorer layout. Documents are edited as numbered rows, and a document can now span several lines (separated by a blank line, where before it was one per line). Results show each document's rank, a score bar and how many places it moved. When Top N is set, the documents below it stay visible, dimmed, under a cut line. Provider and model selection now use the ai_provider_configuration form element, runs are stored with run history, and each run gets a generated code example. Several bugs in the old explorer are fixed, including provider-specific guessing of the result shape.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: ReRankOutput constructor takes an optional fourth argument $rawOutput; getRawOutput() returns it, falling back to the normalized results when it is NULL.

Technical details

RerankGenerator now extends the run-based explorer flow: submitForm() calls executeRun(), builds a ReRankInput, and stores a ranking (index and score per result) and the normalized response in the run output. readRanking() reads the normalized output as described by ReRankInterface: each result is an array or object with an index and a relevance_score or score. It drops results with an invalid or repeated index, and the document text always comes from the documents that were sent, not from the provider's result. This replaces the per-provider shape guessing. If no result points to a document, the run fails with an error.

rankRows() appends documents the provider did not return as unranked rows under the cut. A Top N equal to or greater than the document count is sent as 0, meaning all. Score bars use the raw score when it is within 0 to 1; otherwise they span the run's lowest to highest score, with a hint shown. Documents are parsed by parseDocuments(), which splits on blank lines. The textarea stays the real form value, so the form works without JavaScript. The new js/explorers/rerank.js shows numbered, growing rows (add, remove, paste splitting, screen reader announcements) and keeps the textarea in sync, and explorer.rerank in the libraries file loads it with css/explorers/rerank.css.

The code example is built per run with the shared CodeExample builder, so the query is no longer HTML-escaped into the PHP. ReRankOutput::getRawOutput() used to return the normalized results. It now returns a new optional constructor argument $rawOutput when a provider passes it, and falls back to the results otherwise, so existing providers behave as before.

item.title: #3601420: Create the snap Firefox profile before trusting DDEV's local CA on a fresh Linux desktop
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +115/−4 · bats +82 · sh +32/−3 · md +1/−1
  • Diff: 5c2c646
  • Discussion: #3601420 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

On a fresh Linux desktop where snap Firefox has never been opened, the installer now starts Firefox once in headless mode so it creates its profile. The DDEV local CA is then added to that profile. Before, the CA step found no profile and printed manual import steps. The site then opened in a Firefox that did not trust the CA, and showed "Warning: Potential Security Risk Ahead". macOS is unchanged.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The change is in src/lib/platform/ensure_local_https.sh. _trust_snap_browsers now calls the new _snap_firefox_first_run before its loop. That function returns early unless snap Firefox is installed, certutil and firefox are on the PATH, and no ~/snap/firefox/common/.mozilla/firefox/*/cert9.db exists yet. Otherwise it runs timeout 60 firefox --headless --screenshot ~/snap/firefox/common/oli-first-run.png about:blank and removes the screenshot. A failure or timeout is ignored. If no store exists afterwards, the existing manual import message is printed. Firefox creates its own default profile, rather than the installer using -CreateProfile or certutil -N.

A new helper, _snap_installed, checks for /snap/bin/<name>. The browser loop now uses it as well as the ~/snap/<name> directory check, because that directory only appears after a snap's first run. An installed but never opened snap Chromium therefore gets the manual import instructions instead of being skipped silently. Bats tests cover the headless run, the screenshot cleanup, an existing profile, a failed first run, missing certutil, macOS and the Chromium case. AGENTS.md was updated to match.

item.title: #3586780: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Text Classification Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 7 files, +768/−172 · php +636/−171 · js +78 · css +43 · yml +10 · md +1/−1
  • Diff: e25bf3b
  • Discussion: #3586780 · 1 contributor · 12 comments

Summary

The Text Classification Explorer in AI API Explorer has been rebuilt on the shared explorer layout. Labels are entered as removable chips with one click presets (Sentiment, Support topic, Spam check), and results show as score bars ranked best label first. The long usage paragraph above the text field is gone in favour of a plain "Text" label. The generated PHP example now escapes the text and labels, so quotes and backslashes no longer break the snippet. Runs are stored and listed through the explorer run history when it is enabled.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

TextClassificationGenerator now builds on buildLayout() and replaces AiProviderFormHelper::generateAiProvidersForm() with providerElement('text_classification', ...), the ai_provider_configuration element. Submission goes through executeRun(): it calls textClassification() and stores label/score items, sorted by score with unscored labels last. A response with no items is treated as a failed run ("The provider returned no labels."). Run cards are rendered from the stored run via runTitle(), runBadge(), buildRunOutput() (using ExplorerUi::bars()) and buildRunCode(). The submitted text is passed through Html::escape() before display.

Labels use ExplorerUi::labelChips(), which falls back to a plain one per line textarea without JavaScript. parseLabels() trims lines and drops blanks and case-insensitive duplicates. The new explorer.text_classification library adds js/explorers/text_classification.js (presets, aria-pressed state, run button label showing the label count) and css/explorers/text_classification.css. The code example is built with the shared CodeExample builder, which fixes the unescaped text and labels. The commit also adds a test-only TestTextClassificationProvider in ai_api_explorer_test and a functional TextClassificationExplorerTest. The docs now give the explorer path as /admin/config/ai/explorers/text_classification_generator.

item.title: #3586404: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Embeddings Generation Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +2082/−164 · php +1535/−163 · css +396 · js +144 · yml +6 · md +1/−1
  • Diff: 73efff3
  • Discussion: #3586404 · 1 contributor · 14 comments

Summary

The Embeddings explorer in AI API Explorer is rebuilt on the shared explorer layout. It has two modes: One text, and Compare. Compare embeds up to ten texts and shows a similarity matrix, plus a ranked "nearest to" list for any chosen text. Results now show dimensions, token count and a short vector preview instead of printing the whole vector. The full vector or embeddings matrix can be opened, copied or downloaded as JSON. One text can take an optional image, but only for models that say they read images. Models that read text only, or do not say, get an error and the image is not sent. Runs are stored in run history, and the explorer still works when history is off. Two bugs are fixed: provider_id and model_id from the URL query now select the model, where before they were written to the Text to speech fields. The generated code example no longer calls the non-existent getRaw() and uses a valid image MIME type.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

EmbeddingsGenerator now builds on buildLayout() and the run history helpers (executeRun(), buildRunResults()). Provider and model selection uses the ai_provider_configuration element, through providerElement('embeddings', ...) and createProviderFromValue(), in place of AiProviderFormHelper::generateAiProvidersForm(). The queryProvider() method turns provider_id and model_id into a value for that element. queryTexts() accepts input as a plain string or a JSON list, and a list opens Compare mode.

Compare makes one embeddings() call per text and checks that all vectors have the same length. similarityMatrix() computes cosine similarity for every pair. The result is saved on the run (dimensions, items, matrix, vectors), and the full vectors are also saved as an embeddings.json file for download. Token usage is read from the raw output when the provider reports it. The image path calls readsImages() and throws unless the model reports image support. A model that does not say is treated as unable to read images, because such providers drop the image and embed the text alone. Per-model facts such as vector size and image support go to the browser as data-aie-embeddings-models.

New assets: the explorer.embeddings library (css/explorers/embeddings.css, js/explorers/embeddings.js). The JS behaviors handle adding and removing text rows, switching the image fieldset on and off with the chosen model, and showing the nearest list of the selected text. The commit also adds functional and FunctionalJavascript tests and updates the explorer docs path to /admin/config/ai/explorers/embeddings_generator. The diff tool omitted EmbeddingsGenerator.php, so this section was read from the file in the repository, where later commits may also have touched it.

item.title: #3586405: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Translate Text Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 10 files, +670/−222 · php +587/−221 · css +38 · js +33 · yml +11 · md +1/−1
  • Diff: c0e9c97
  • Discussion: #3586405 · 1 contributor · 15 comments

Summary

The Translate Text Explorer in the AI API Explorer module has been rebuilt on the shared explorer layout. Source and target languages are now selects showing language names (the source defaults to "Detect automatically"), a swap button exchanges them, and the provider and model are chosen through the ai_provider_configuration element. Each run appears under Results with the source text, the translation, the detected language, a copy button and a generated PHP code example. Previously there was no code example, and provider metadata could print as "Array" with a PHP warning; an empty translation now shows as an error on the run.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

TranslationGenerator now builds its form with buildLayout() and providerElement('translate_text', ...) instead of AiProviderFormHelper::generateAiProvidersForm(). Submission goes through executeRun(), which stores each run (when run history is enabled) and renders Results from stored runs via buildRunResults(), buildRunOutput(), runBadge() and buildRunCode(). If history is off the explorer still works. The target is a single language per run. When the source is empty, NULL is passed to TranslateTextInput so the provider detects it.

The detected language is read from the output metadata key detected_source_language by the new static detectedLanguage(), which accepts a plain code, a list of codes, or an array with language or code. This replaces the old string cast of metadata. An empty translation throws a RuntimeException with a translated message, shown as an error run. Language names come from LanguageManager::getStandardLanguageList(). Code examples are built with CodeExample.

A new library explorer.translate (css/explorers/translate.css, js/explorers/translate.js) is attached explicitly, because the layout's automatic library name would be explorer.translation. The aieTranslateSwap behavior enables the swap button only when a source language is selected. The tests add a TestTranslateProvider (ai_api_explorer_test_translate) in ai_api_explorer_test, plus functional, JavaScript and unit tests, and the old TranslationGeneratorTest unit test is removed. The docs page now gives the path /admin/config/ai/explorers/translation_generator.

item.title: #3586413: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Image-To-Image Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 7 files, +3180/−203 · php +2044/−203 · js +712 · css +415 · yml +9
  • Diff: 7c01edd
  • Discussion: #3586413 · 1 contributor · 12 comments

Summary

The Image-To-Image Explorer is redesigned on the shared explorer layout. You pick a source image (recent results, media library or upload), then a task: edit with a prompt, remove background, fill an area, or upscale. Only the settings relevant to the task and to the selected model are shown. For "Fill an area" you can paint the mask in a full-screen editor (brush, eraser, size, undo, invert, clear) instead of uploading a mask file. Results are stored as runs with before/after comparison, and failed runs keep an error with Retry. Provider and model selection now use the ai_provider_configuration element. A new "Flatten transparency onto white" option (on by default) addresses transparent PNG sources producing mostly empty edits.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New explorer.image_to_image asset library and a TestImageToImageProvider (ai_api_explorer_test_image_to_image) test provider in ai_api_explorer_test.

Technical details

ImageToImageGenerator was rewritten around buildLayout() and executeRun(), replacing AiProviderFormHelper::generateAiProvidersForm() with providerElement('image_to_image', ...), with modelDetails() as the capability details callback. The source uses the ai_api_explorer_file element. validateRun() runs only for the aie_run trigger and checks the per-task prompt, rejects JPEG with a transparent background, and validates the painted mask: it must be a PNG data URL up to 20 MB and match the source image dimensions, so a provider does not reject it after a paid upload. Provider creation now goes through createProviderFromValue() inside the run callback, so failures are recorded on the run instead of thrown. Task settings are mapped to the model's getAvailableConfiguration() through resolveSettings(); settings the model does not list are reported as skipped. Result files are saved through runManager()->saveFile() with the MIME type taken from the image data, falling back to a known image type, so returned SVG or HTML is not served as claimed. The code example per run comes from the shared CodeExample builder.

The client side is in js/explorers/image_to_image.js and css/explorers/image_to_image.css, attached through the new explorer.image_to_image library. The mask editor is a <dialog> with a canvas. It keeps strokes as a list of steps so undo replays them. It exports an opaque black PNG with the painted areas transparent into the hidden mask_data field, and clears the mask if the source image changes. Retry presses the run button of the picked task. Tests add a TestImageToImageProvider (models greyscale, inpainter, upscaler) plus kernel and FunctionalJavascript tests.

item.title: #3586417: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Audio-To-Audio Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +1768/−184 · php +1606/−180 · css +90 · js +58 · yml +9 · md +5/−4
  • Diff: 282ef3e
  • Discussion: #3586417 · 1 contributor · 12 comments

Summary

The Audio to Audio Explorer in AI API Explorer is rebuilt on the shared explorer layout. You pick a task (remove noise, restore phone audio, isolate voice) and only that task's options show. Results show the original next to the result in players, with the option to use a result as the source for another run. Runs that previously always failed with a "Configuration Error" now complete, and the generated code example is corrected.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The plugin AudioToAudioGenerator drops AiProviderFormHelper::generateAiProvidersForm() and uses the ai_provider_configuration element through providerElement('audio_to_audio', ...). File input is the shared ai_api_explorer_file element. Each run goes through executeRun(), so it is stored as an explorer run and results are rendered from stored runs by buildRunOutput(), with a per run code example from buildRunCode() using the shared CodeExample builder. New assets explorer.audio_to_audio (css/explorers/audio_to_audio.css, js/explorers/audio_to_audio.js) are registered in ai_api_explorer.libraries.yml; the JS only switches the run button label and hint per task.

The old failure came from passing the AudioFile[] returned by getNormalized() straight to saveData(). The new code treats every normalized item as its own file and saves each with runManager()->saveFile(), so a model that splits audio can return two files. The result file's extension and MIME type follow the audio the provider returns, with a notice when it differs from the requested format.

The audio to audio operation takes only the audio, so the task options (strength, keep room sound, sample rate, which part to keep, output format) are sent through the provider configuration. mapOptions() matches each option to a model configuration key from OPTION_KEYS (for example strength, noise_reduction, denoise_strength) only when that field can take the value (fieldTakes()). Matched fields are hidden from the model's own settings; options the model has no usable setting for are listed in a notice on the run, and the model uses its own value.

The docs page for the explorer is updated: the example uses audio/mpeg instead of audio/mp3 and reads getNormalized()[0], and the explorer path and name are corrected.

item.title: #3586409: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Moderation Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +613/−123 · php +572/−122 · css +34 · yml +6 · md +1/−1
  • Diff: 4b8a97f
  • Discussion: #3586409 · 1 contributor · 11 comments

Summary

The Moderation Explorer (part of the AI API Explorer module) has a new layout shared with the other redesigned explorers. Each check now shows a clear Flagged or Not flagged verdict with the highest-scoring category, and every category score as a bar, highest first, with flagged categories in red. The field is labelled "Text to check" and the button reads "Check text" instead of "Ask The AI". Each check is stored as a run, so results can be kept across reloads when run history is enabled. The generated code example is now correct: it previously used an undefined $input variable.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

ModerationGenerator now builds on the shared shell from AiApiExplorerPluginBase (buildLayout(), runButton(), executeRun(), buildRunResults()), replacing the old getFormTemplate() and AiProviderFormHelper::generateAiProvidersForm() flow with the ai_provider_configuration element via providerElement('moderation', ...). Submission creates a ModerationInput, calls moderation(), and stores flagged state, scores, flags, the provider message and token usage on the run. Results are rendered from stored runs (buildRunCard(), buildRunOutput()), and the code example is generated per run with the shared CodeExample builder in buildRunCode().

Providers return scores in different shapes, so findScores() handles both a flat category to score map (OpenAI style, with per-category flags read from the raw response's results[0].categories) and a nested categories array with probability or score and its own flagged. Only values between 0 and 1 count as scores. When no scores can be found, the raw information is shown as key/value details instead. Category names are made readable (for example harassment/threatening becomes "Harassment, threatening") and scores under 0.001 show as <0.001.

Styles live in a new css/explorers/moderation.css, registered as the explorer.moderation library in ai_api_explorer.libraries.yml. A new ModerationExplorerTest functional test uses the ai_test mock provider to cover the flagged and not-flagged cases, nested categories, and the code example. The docs page for the moderation operation now points to the correct explorer path /admin/config/ai/explorers/moderation_generator.

item.title: #3586410: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Object Detection Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +951/−206 · php +838/−206 · css +80 · js +24 · yml +9
  • Diff: 3abf58b
  • Discussion: #3586410 · 1 contributor · 13 comments

Summary

The Object Detection Explorer in the AI API Explorer module has been rebuilt on the shared explorer layout. Previously it showed detected objects only as numbers in a table and never displayed the image. Now the uploaded image is shown with a box for each detected object, labelled with its name and score, and there is a Boxes/Table switch. A minimum confidence slider sets which boxes start visible (lower-scoring ones stay in the response), and results are stored as runs with a code example generated per run.

Impact

item.title: #3601419: Trust DDEV’s local CA in snap Firefox and Chromium on Linux
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +116/−13 · bats +71/−2 · sh +43/−10 · txt +1 · md +1/−1
  • Diff: ad3fd9d
  • Discussion: #3601419 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

On Linux desktops where Firefox or Chromium is installed as a snap (the Ubuntu default), the installer now adds DDEV's local certificate authority directly to the browser's own certificate store. Previously mkcert -install could not reach that store, so https://<project>.ddev.site still showed a security warning. After the installer runs, restart the browser if it is open. A snap browser that has never been opened has no certificate store yet, so the installer still prints the manual import steps for it.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

_warn_snap_browsers in src/lib/platform/ensure_local_https.sh is replaced by _trust_snap_browsers, called from ensure_local_https on Linux after mkcert -install. For each of ~/snap/firefox and ~/snap/chromium that exists, it collects NSS database directories: every ~/snap/firefox/common/.mozilla/firefox/*/ containing cert9.db, and ~/snap/chromium/current/.pki/nssdb if it has cert9.db. The new helper _add_ca_to_nss_dbs runs certutil -A -d "sql:<dir>" -t "C,," -n "mkcert development CA (DDEV)" -i "$(mkcert -CAROOT)/rootCA.pem" on each one, and fails if certutil is missing or any add fails.

The issue proposed skipping databases that already hold the CA, but the code does not check first. A comment in the code says re-adding the same CA is harmless. Browsers that were updated print an ok message asking for a restart. Browsers with no database, or where certutil fails, print the existing warning with manual import instructions. The function always returns 0, so the step stays best-effort. New bats tests cover multiple Firefox profiles, the Chromium nssdb, no-profile, missing certutil, a failing certutil -A, and macOS. AGENTS.md and the spelling dictionary (nssdb) are updated.

item.title: #3586778: Shared AI API Explorer input picker: recent results, media library or upload
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 12 files, +2428/−0 · php +1836 · css +309 · js +263 · yml +20
  • Diff: 1291c9d
  • Discussion: #3586778 · 1 contributor · 22 comments

Summary

The AI API Explorer module gets a shared input picker for explorers that take an image or audio file. The user can choose a recent result from their own explorer runs, pick an item from the media library, or upload a file. A preview shows the chosen file with its type, size, and dimensions or length. Without run history the recent results are not shown. If Media or Media Library is off, the media option is replaced by a note giving the reason, or by a plain media autocomplete when only Media Library is missing. The commit shows the element working in a test explorer. The diff I could read does not show the existing file-input explorers being switched to it.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New ai_api_explorer_file form element (Drupal\ai_api_explorer\Element\ExplorerFile) with ExplorerFile::toOperationFile(), plus a media_library.opener service and an ai_api_explorer.file_forget route.

Technical details

The picker is a new form element, ExplorerFile (#type ai_api_explorer_file), in modules/ai_api_explorer/src/Element/ExplorerFile.php. Its value is ['fid' => ..., 'source' => 'recent'|'media'|'upload']. Properties are #media_type (image, audio or video), #operation_type, #extensions, #recent and #media. Accepted extensions come from #extensions, else from the OPERATION_EXTENSIONS map for the operation type (for example speech_to_text audio: mp3 m4a mp4 wav webm ogg flac), else from per-media-type defaults. Every source goes through ExplorerFile::accepts(), which checks extension and MIME type. A recent result or media item therefore cannot bring in a format that an upload would be refused for. MP4 and WebM files that Drupal detects as video are allowed as audio.

On validation, a recent or uploaded file must belong to the current user and the user needs access ai prompt. Uploads must also be files stored by the explorers (isRunFile()). Media items must pass access('view') and belong to a media type whose source is the right kind. ExplorerFile::toOperationFile() turns the file entity into an ImageFile, AudioFile, VideoFile or GenericFile carrying the file's real MIME type.

When Media Library is enabled, a new AiApiExplorerServiceProvider registers ExplorerFileOpener as a media_library.opener. It returns the picked item to the picker by AJAX and refuses files the picker does not accept. A required picker with no default value takes the ?file= query parameter, which is how "Use as source" links can preselect a file. This only works for the user's own files stored by the explorers. A new ai_api_explorer.file_forget POST route and a hover button on the thumbnails let users remove a file from recent files. A file library (explorer-file.js and explorer-file.css) drives the preview and the clear and remove buttons. The commit also adds a PickerTestExplorer in ai_api_explorer_test, which calls useAsSourceLink() from the plugin base class. Kernel and functional tests were added but were not in the diff I could read.

Upgrade

Explorer plugin authors can replace a custom upload field with the element:

$form['setup']['image'] = [
  '#type' => 'ai_api_explorer_file',
  '#title' => $this->t('Source image'),
  '#media_type' => 'image',
  '#extensions' => 'png jpg jpeg',
  '#required' => TRUE,
];

Then on submit, turn the picked file into an operation input:

$value = $form_state->getValue('image');
$operation_file = ExplorerFile::toOperationFile(File::load($value['fid']));

Summary

The AI API Explorers page at /admin/config/ai/explorers is now a hub of cards grouped by type (Text, Search and ranking, Image, Audio and video, Tools and more). Each card shows the explorer name, description and the providers that can serve it. Explorers with no usable provider stay in the list, dimmed, with a "No provider yet · Set up" label instead of disappearing. There is a search box, type filters and an "Only ready to use" checkbox. A provider that throws while the page checks which providers are usable no longer takes the page down: a notice and a per-card warning appear and the error is logged. An explorer that fails to load is shown as a broken card and logged, and a router rebuild no longer fails because of it.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: The explorers list is rendered by the new ai-api-explorer-hub.html.twig template instead of the core admin block list.
  • API change: ExplorerSetupList controller removed in favor of ExplorerHub; AiApiExplorerAccessChecker constructor now takes a logger.

The route ai_api_explorer.list_page now points to the new ExplorerHub::build() controller, which replaces ExplorerSetupList and its SystemManager::getBlockContents() output. Provider usability comes from the ai_api_explorer.availability service (getProviders(), getFailures()), and cards use getHubSummary() when an explorer plugin provides one. It takes the route title from the plugin definition, so a plugin that throws in create() cannot break a router rebuild. item.description:

Summary

The AI API Explorer now has shared viewers for file results. An audio player draws a waveform and has play/pause, click-to-seek, a speed button, duration and download. Formats browsers cannot play, such as raw PCM, show a note and a download link instead. Images open full size in a dialog with their details and a download link, and transparent images sit on a checkerboard. There is also a before/after image comparison with a slider or side-by-side mode, and a box overlay with a minimum-confidence slider and label toggles. A style guide explorer in the test module shows each viewer with sample files. Explorers such as text to speech, text to image and object detection can use these viewers without writing their own markup.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Six new Twig templates (ai-api-explorer-*.html.twig) that themes can override.
  • New API: New theme hooks ai_api_explorer_audio, ai_api_explorer_image, ai_api_explorer_compare, ai_api_explorer_boxes, ai_api_explorer_audio_compare and ai_api_explorer_bars, with templates and an ai_api_explorer/media library.

Technical details

The commit registers the theme hooks in Hook\AiApiExplorer, each with an initial preprocess function in ai_api_explorer.module. Each has a Twig template, and the audio and image templates take their icons from ExplorerUi::icon(). The matching ExplorerUi builder methods (audio(), image(), audioCompare(), compare(), boxes(), bars()) already existed in the module. Each one attaches the new ai_api_explorer/media library, which depends on explorer_ui and adds css/explorer-media.css and js/explorer-media.js.

The preprocess functions do the computation. For boxes, pixel coordinates become percentages of the image size, and the box labels are counted for the toggle buttons. For bars, values are clamped between 0 and 1 and given CSS classes. Image and compare templates get an aspect-ratio from width and height when both are known.

The behaviors in explorer-media.js are aieAudioPlayer, aieCompare and aieBoxes. The audio player fetches the file once and decodes it with the Web Audio API to get waveform peaks. It then plays the same blob through an object URL, which it revokes on detach. If the fetch or decode fails, the <audio> element loads the URL itself, and an error event or a failed play() switches the player to a note plus download. Starting one player pauses the others. The compare slider and the confidence control are native input[type=range] elements, so they work with the keyboard. Image preview uses a native <dialog> opened through data-aie-dialog-open. The dialog handler is not part of this diff.

The test module gets a styleguide_explorer plugin with sample SVG, WAV and PNG assets. Functional and kernel tests cover the new markup and theme hooks. A FunctionalJavascript test was also added, but its diff was not available to me.

Upgrade

To use the viewers, return the ExplorerUi render arrays from an explorer plugin, as the style guide plugin does:

'player' => ExplorerUi::audio($assets . 'sample.wav', 'audio/wav', 'sample.wav', $this->t('the sample')),
'compare' => ExplorerUi::compare($assets . 'before.svg', $assets . 'after.svg', ['width' => 640, 'height' => 420]),
